=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26874-26878 | severity=critical | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The guard clears `merge_head_ref` when `.head.repo.full_name` is empty and relies on `_pr_ensure_final_ci` to reject a fork head. That helper (scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:1032-1040) rejects only a non-empty repo name that differs from the target, so a deleted-fork PR (null head.repo) gets `ci.yml` dispatched on its head ref in the base repo.
  WHY: Severity disagreement: NIT (sonnet), MAJOR (gemini, minimax, glm), and MAJOR from luna, which claims fork-provided code can run with `GH_TOKEN` available; the highest is recorded here as critical. The README and changelog claim fork heads never get a final-CI dispatch, but the empty-repo case leaks through.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26874-26877; 26912-26936 | severity=major | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Clearing `merge_head_ref` to handle fork repositories is overly permissive. It depends on `_pr_ensure_final_ci` rejecting forks when the ref is empty, and the helper may not do so.
  WHY: The final CI could be dispatched on a base-repo ref name that does not exist there or that belongs to a deleted fork. This overlaps the deleted-fork finding above but is worded as a general logic defect.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26874-26878 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The guard treats an empty head_repo and a fork head_repo the same, but the helper rejects only the non-empty case. The guard therefore has no runtime effect for a deleted-fork PR.
  WHY: The documented claim that the fork-dispatch hole is closed is wrong for the empty head_repo sub-case.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:1478-1481; 1717-1720 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Neither stall-recovery step sets `AUTO_MERGE_REQUIRED_CI_CHECK` (or `AUTO_MERGE_WAIT_WORKFLOWS`). `_pr_wait_for_required_checks` (scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:797) reads the name only from the environment, so the stall path falls back to `lint`, unlike the review auto-merge path.
  WHY: With a custom or disabled required-check variable, the stall path can refuse with `checks_incomplete` and burn recovery budget, or merge when the review path would not. Gemini did not report this.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26867-26873 | severity=major | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: A timeout in `_pr_wait_for_required_checks` while final CI is in flight does not count toward the recovery budget and gives no visibility.
  WHY: If CI is queued or hung, every poll tick returns in-flight with no attempt recorded and no notice, so the issue never escalates to a human.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26920-26933 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The in-flight sub-branch (26927-26928) never increments the recovery count and sends no notification, and nothing bounds how long it can last.
  WHY: A hung CI check can keep the issue in this branch indefinitely, so `escalate_human` is unreachable. The no-increment rule is issue-mandated, but the bound and the notice are missing.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:1478-1481; 1717-1720 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW` is set for the whole poll step, so other callers of the shared wait helper also dispatch `ci.yml`, including the noop-suspicious gate D wait. `STALL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS_ENABLED` does not gate those callers.
  WHY: The effect is wider than the stated gate. The README and changelog document it, but the agents.d fragment does not. GLM adds that a refused dispatch can update an approved PR's branch.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:32634-32661 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `test_standalone_attempt_merge_head_ref_only_for_same_repo_head` checks only that the guard clears `merge_head_ref`. It does not run `_pr_ensure_final_ci`, so the empty-head_repo case has no end-to-end coverage.
  WHY: A change to the guard would still pass the test, and the leak would go unnoticed.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:1481, 1720 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW` applies to every caller of the wait helper in those steps, including the noop-suspicious gate D wait.
  WHY: `STALL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS_ENABLED` does not switch off all of the new final-CI dispatching. The agents.d fragment does not document this.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26874-26878 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The guard clears `merge_head_ref` for an empty head_repo, but `_pr_ensure_final_ci` (scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:1036) rejects only when head_repo is non-empty and differs. A deleted-fork PR then gets `ci.yml` dispatched on a base-repo branch of the same name.
  WHY: The README (line 106) and changelog (line 10) overstate the protection. The case needs a deleted-fork PR plus a ref-name collision, so it is narrow.

- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:32634-32661 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The regression test does not stub or invoke `_pr_ensure_final_ci`, so the empty-head_repo edge case has no end-to-end coverage.
  WHY: A change to the guard would still pass the test, and the leak would not be caught.

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2674-2677; scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:1032-1040; .github/workflows/ci.yml:28-37, 152-168 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When `.head.repo.full_name` is missing, the guard clears `merge_head_ref` and relies on `_pr_ensure_final_ci`, which rejects only a non-empty differing repo name.
  WHY: For a deleted-fork PR whose head ref exists in the base repo, `ci.yml` can be dispatched. It checks out the PR merge ref and runs `ci_final_merge_ref_fresh.sh` with `GH_TOKEN` available, so fork-provided code can execute in the base-repo workflow context.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2694; .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:1480-1481, 1719-1720; scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:795-824 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Neither stall-recovery step passes `AUTO_MERGE_REQUIRED_CI_CHECK` from the repo variable to the new wait call, so the helper uses its default `lint`.
  WHY: With a custom required check, stall recovery can merge when that check is missing or failing. With `none`, it can refuse and spend recovery attempts waiting for `lint`.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===

  WHY: The dispatch runs on an unrelated base-repo branch with the fork PR's `pr_number`/`head_sha` inputs. It is the `fork_head` case the guard was meant to prevent, and it wastes runner slots.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:1478-1481, 1717-1720 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The stall-recovery steps do not pass `AUTO_MERGE_REQUIRED_CI_CHECK` or `AUTO_MERGE_WAIT_WORKFLOWS`, which the review path passes (review_autofix.yml:1208-1209), and the resolver reads only the environment (pr_checks_lib.sh:797).
  WHY: The review and stall gates resolve different required checks. The stall path refuses and burns recovery budget, escalating to `ai:needs-human` on a configuration mismatch.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26920-26933 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The in-flight sub-branch (26927-26928) never counts an attempt, never notifies, and has no time bound.
  WHY: A hung CI check keeps the issue in this branch indefinitely, so `escalate_human` (line 26940) is unreachable. The no-increment rule is issue-mandated.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:1479-1480, 1718-1719 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW` is set for the whole poll step. Other callers of the wait helper, including the noop-suspicious gate D wait (orchestrate_poll_process.sh:36833) and the base-freshness branch update (pr_checks_lib.sh:1167), now also dispatch `ci.yml`.
  WHY: `STALL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS_ENABLED` does not gate those callers, so an approved PR's branch can be updated as a side effect with no separate kill switch.
